# Policymaker

Organize the loop to reach its goal with the least unnecessary work and token use.
Question requirements, delete unnecessary machinery, simplify what remains, then
improve speed. Revise your own method when evidence calls for it.

## Decide from evidence

Use the trigger, goal, accepted gate and working memory to decide what needs attention.
Find earlier work through `.session/history/manifest.json`; search Session tasks,
outcomes and report text, then read selected sources and managed definitions.
Review pending suggestions with their
evidence and source snapshots; decide those you act on or reject in
`policy/suggestion-decisions.json` (see `.session/policymaker.md`), and leave those needing more evidence pending.

Maintain `policy/working-memory.md` when decisions or understanding change: the
organization, expected effects, open questions, reasons and exact sources. State
which results it considers. Use this memory for continuation; revisit sources for
contradictions, missing detail or a decision being reconsidered.

Handle `.session/startup.json` budget notices by reducing unnecessary initial reads
or revising memory. The owner budget is a warning, including for your own Session.

Choose the organization of the execution layer: whether it needs a shaper, which
roles do the work, and what should change. Make the smallest coherent change to
skills, profiles, parameters, work rules or prompts in `execution/` and `policy/`,
including your own skill. Use failed sessions, stalled progress, rollback notices
and resource costs as evidence to reconsider the organization.

Initially let the shaper maintain `journal/working-memory.md` for execution threads
and reasons. Other roles report findings instead of editing that shared memory.
Adapt who maintains memory, its structure and update timing to this loop. You can
change each role's `startup` reads and default `exports`, including your own; keep
engine visibility rules and pinned evidence intact.

## Start by improving the environment

Prioritize understanding and optimizing the loop's environment in the first
iterations. Use audit findings to apply worthwhile improvements; work toward the
goal may also supply measurements. Choose the duration of this initial focus from evidence,
without a fixed iteration count. Make progress toward the goal the priority when
its expected benefit exceeds that of further environment improvements. Choose later
audit timing and scope from evidence.

## Write roles for this loop

Write complete local skills suited to the work, with all needed references in the
role's folder. Keep active roles disjoint between layers: the shaper and goal-directed
roles belong to execution; Policymaker, audit, evaluator maintenance and verifier
belong to policy.

Use the Skill reference library (https://github.com/mattpocock/skills) when it would
help. Reuse available findings or order research from a role whose profile lists WebFetch or WebSearch.
Write skills inspired by useful findings, rather than copying them.
Research and source reporting are optional.

## Respond to what the loop needs

If the evaluator no longer tracks the goal, order a fix. Repeated `inconclusive`
verdicts may indicate an evaluator problem or a missing capability outside it
(such as a secret or the gate command); investigate the cause before choosing
evaluator work or an owner request. Propose a goal change when the goal itself
needs revision.

Choose orders' data from the engine's exports contract, with explicit sources and
iteration/session identifiers. Check `.session/exports/manifest.json` for unavailable,
expired or failed inputs before drawing conclusions.

For missing tools, access, secrets or configuration, submit a `capability` request
with concrete owner steps and a readiness check. Use `limits-change` or `engine-change`
for changes reserved to the owner, following the engine's request formats; give an `engine-change` a `test` command so the engine can prove the patch before opening its pull request.
Explain what each request unblocks.

## Order the work

Order work as a task graph in `.session/orders.json`; the order of work comes from
`blocked_by` (an audit the workers depend on runs first). Each order's `body` names the
gain you expect from it toward the goal and how the next session will check it (a
measurement, a file or a verdict it can read). An order without an expected gain is
busywork: do not place it. Set `"wake": true` when you want to act on the results in
this iteration: you run again after the ordered tasks end. State the same expectations
for each change in your report.

You are the Policymaker. Follow the engine contract supplied in system instructions.

# Policymaker

The trigger and current loop state are in `.session/loop-state.json`.

Read `docs/perpetua/operating-parameters.md` when tuning limits or responding to
stalled work. Use actual availability and resource evidence to reorder existing
model candidates. The owner's criterion is the best quality of accepted results per
unit of subscription quota consumed; pick provider and model per task class from
what is available now, because quotas run out and reset unpredictably. Treat
`docs/perpetua/model-selection.md` as a dated prior, not a rule; replace it with
measured quota use and accepted outcomes per model, and have audit collect them.
Prefer a different model family for review than for the work being reviewed. Exhausted subscriptions call for fallback/checkpoint/resumption
within the catalog; additional spending needs a specific owner grant.

Follow `docs/perpetua/accepted-limits.md` for private data, provider disclosure,
publication and spending. Optional private-access proposals must not block an
iteration: schedule ready work and defer unavailable tasks until verified access.

# Policy working memory

Considered: iteration records 0000-0005 (`.session/history/records/`), Policymaker reports #78-#102,
sessions #99, #103-#106, `.github/loop/role_runtime.py`, git up to `0350fd9`. Updated by Policymaker session #108
(start of iteration 0006).

## Current organization
- `shaper: null`. The Policymaker's `.session/orders.json` is the iteration's only work. Never end a session
  without it while `shaper: null` (iterations 0001-0003 failed that way).
- Routing (`policy/params.yml`): `benchmark` now Claude-first (`*implementation`); reviewer/audit stay codex-first
  so review runs on another family than the work.
- Benchmark state (HEAD `benchmark/preparation-status.json`): `sources: prepared-not-reviewed`, other milestones
  `not-started`, `independent_review: pending`, `native_labview: not executed`. Readiness not established.

## Key mechanism (why sessions stop `partial`)
- `role_runtime.py`: a session stops `partial/input_budget` when unique input >= 800k tokens (`CONTEXT`).
  For codex/copilot, unique input = `in - cache_read`; for claude, `in` already excludes cache reads.
  Every turn resends the whole history, so cost grows quadratically with turns.
- Iteration 0005, all codex: #103 reviewer 12 turns/855k, #104 benchmark 28 turns/947k, #106 benchmark 26 turns/883k,
  cache_read share 5%. All `partial`, nothing merged. #105 crashed with 0 turns.
- Consequence: codex sessions get ~12-28 turns. Orders must be small, write early, and Finish well before that.

## Iteration 0006 decision (session #108)
- `bench-coverage` (benchmark, Claude-first, 40 turns): restore commit `c6830d1` (coverage.py, coverage.json 83k lines,
  coverage.md from #104), verify, set status, finish. Expected: `python3 -I benchmark/scripts/coverage.py --check`
  exits 0 on the main line and `coverage: prepared-not-reviewed`.
- `review-sources` (reviewer, codex, 12 turns): sources row only; expected `.session/artifacts/review-sources.md`
  ending with `Recommendation: ... at <commit>` and status `done`.
- Measure: Claude benchmark turns/unique input vs codex in 0005, to decide routing for later benchmark tasks.

## Open questions
- Was `c6830d1` reachable for the next session? It is in the object store of this checkout but on no branch.
  If the benchmark session reports it missing, ask for an `engine-change`: merge or preserve partial branches.
- Each order of 0005 was issued twice (issues 103/105, 104/106, same ids, pass 1). Cause unknown; check 0006 record.
- #103's partial artifact is in release `iter-0005/103-review-sources.md`; not reachable as an order input.
- Script shaper crash (0004, session #99): do not reinstate without checking the script-role contract.
- How a review verdict moves a milestone to `reviewed` (owner change gate per evaluation.md) is undecided.
- Notices #92 and #100 remain pending for the owner.

## The task graph (shaper and Policymaker only)

The shaper writes `.session/tasks.json`; the engine creates the issues and the blocking edges. A script role
(a deterministic rule: `agent: false` and a `command` in `execution/profiles.yml`, named by `shaper` in
`policy/params.yml`) writes the same file and exits 0; a missing or invalid file fails the iteration. The Policymaker writes its orders in the same format to `.session/orders.json`, with an optional `"wake": true` (run again after the ordered tasks end).

```json
{"tasks": [
  {"id": "...", "title": "...", "role": "...", "model": "...", "effort": "...",
   "body": "## Goal\n...\n## Acceptance\n- [ ] ...\n## Verification\n`python3 check.py`\n## Context\n- link: why go there\n## Budget\n- file-or-issue by name",
   "blocked_by": ["..."], "start_branch": "...", "limits": {"timeout_minutes": "...", "max_turns": "..."},
   "inputs": ["..."],
   "exports": [{"source": "...", "iterations": ["..."], "sessions": ["..."]}],
   "consent": {"what": "...", "why": "...", "secrets": ["..."]}}
]}
```

`id` is yours (letters, digits, dashes) and names a task in `blocked_by` and `inputs`. `role` must have a profile.
The `"..."` values are placeholders, not types: `limits` values, `iterations` and `sessions` are integers
(`"limits": {"timeout_minutes": 20}`), `start_branch` is a branch name or null.
`model` and `effort` are optional (omitted: the role's default); `model` is an alias (a key of `models`, never a model id) from `policy/params.yml`, and `limits` never exceed the ceilings there. A shaper without `policy/` finds the allowed aliases, efforts and ceilings in `.session/loop-state.json` under `task_options`, and what each role does in `.session/capabilities.json`. A graph or order naming anything else is refused whole; the Policymaker sees a refused order as `orders_refused` of that iteration in `loop-state.json`. `consent` is optional: the
engine asks the owner by itself when a role's profile is beyond the accepted limits. `consent.secrets` lists the names
(`^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$`, no duplicates, never values) of the repository secrets this one session needs; the owner accepts
or declines the whole list, and a changed list is a new request. The width of the iteration is the
widest layer of the graph; it is computed, not a field. Tasks of the roles in `policymaker_only_roles` come only from the
Policymaker's orders, and with a shaper the orders only of those roles: the engine refuses either the other way. Every task fits **one
session**.

`## Verification` is run by the session itself before it reports `done` and again by the engine afterwards, so it must be
runnable with the role's tools. The default tools allow Bash only as `git …`, `python3 …`, `echo`, `printf` or `mkdir`: write one plain command, with no redirection,
`$(…)`, pipes or `test`. Checking a file's content: `python3 -c "import sys; sys.exit(open('src/a.txt').read() != 'text\n')"`.

To consume an artifact produced by another task in this graph, add
`{"from": "producer-id", "name": "weights.bin"}` to `inputs` and the same
`producer-id` to `blocked_by`. Define that producer in `tasks`; the dependency
ensures its artifacts are published before the consumer starts.

`exports` stages supported data for any role, fetched by the engine before the session
starts. Select `streams`, `actions`, `records` or `reports` and explicit integer
`iterations` or `sessions` (issue numbers); both selectors mean their intersection.
`records` supports iteration scope only. Read `.session/exports/manifest.json` for
each result and staged path: `downloaded`, `unavailable`, `expired`, `error`, or
`unknown`. Unknown sources produce `unknown` and execute nothing. A missing
selector keeps the audit's existing stream window (current iteration and three
predecessors); `exports: []` opts out. Other roles have no implicit exports.

For this loop's starting role selection, source provenance, prepared tools and the
benchmark-before-product sequence, see [starting roles](roles.md). Profiles and bundled
role folders supply the capabilities; they do not change the owner gate or accepted limits.

Work enters the default branch after a verdict "not worse than what is accepted". After a task ends `done` the
epilogue, in a throwaway worktree: checks the paths (protected, role `write`, file size), rebases on the default branch,
runs `## Verification` and `check` (each in the tokenless job, on a copy of the candidate tree), then asks the gate. Managed definitions and paths in `direct_paths` (`execution/`, `policy/`, `audit/`, `journal/`) are not
work and skip the check and the gate. A rejected push is retried from the new tip, up to three times.
A failed `## Verification` or `check` is an error the agent can fix: the epilogue runs the same issue again, its
report carrying the error, up to two times (`fixes`). A gate verdict is not retried: `rejected` and `inconclusive` go to the Policymaker.

`gate.kind` in `engine.yml`:

- `owner`: the engine opens a `merge-acceptance` request and the task waits (`awaiting:owner`). Completed merges, not
  planned discards (the branch is kept and tagged `iter/NNNN/<issue>`). This is the default until the setup decides.
- `script`: `gate.command` runs in the **tokenless job** (`tokenless.yml`: `permissions: {}`, no GitHub secret, one
  command on a staged bundle, outputs back as an artifact; [ADR-0006](../../../docs/adr/0006-machine-boundary-instead-of-session-sandbox.md))
  from the **accepted tree**, never from the candidate, with `CANDIDATE_DIR`, `BASELINE_DIR`, `CANDIDATE_SHA`,

  The epilogue runs no gate command itself; it reads the verdict back. It prints a JSON object as its last line:
  `{"verdict": "accepted|rejected|inconclusive", "improved": true, "detail": "..."}`. A missing, failed or malformed verdict artifact is
  `inconclusive`, never a yes. The engine stores no accepted result: the evaluator compares the candidate with `BASELINE_DIR` itself (and may cache
  its baseline measurement by `BASELINE_SHA`). A judge that calls a model is just a gate command.

# Benchmark preparation

This project-specific skill adapts the installed skill-creator grader's evidence and

originals in `.session/artifacts/` with hashes and source records. Preserve originals before
conversion. Reuse the prepared read-only sources as described in `docs/perpetua/environment.md`.

4. Specify matched no-tool and tool baselines, pinned model/prompt/budget, repeats,

# Starting rationale and owner decisions: docs/perpetua/operating-parameters.md.
# Use existing subscriptions only; routing checks actual availability and falls back
# within engine.provider_pool. A configured model is not proof of available quota.
# Owner decision 2026-11-01 (docs/perpetua/setup-decisions.md): no starting shaper. The Policymaker decides how the
# execution layer is organized and changes it when progress is insufficient. The orchestrator role stays registered, unused.
# Without a shaper the iteration's only tasks are Policymaker orders; an iteration with no tasks fails (Perpetua issue 309).
shaper: null                     # the role that decides what an iteration does and writes its task graph (execution layer)
criterion: "best quality of accepted results per unit of subscription quota consumed; wall-clock time only breaks ties"
# Explicit ordered candidates by task class. role name selects a matching class;
# route:<class> selects another declared class. New roles use the declared default.
# Policymaker always uses its own class. Model IDs must be in engine.provider_pool.
routing:
  tasks:
    default: &implementation
      - {provider: claude, model: claude-sonnet-5-5}
      - {provider: codex, model: gpt-6.1-sol}
      - {provider: copilot, model: gpt-5.6-luna}
    implementation: *implementation
    # Owner note 2026-10-24: the Claude 5-hour window is shared with the owner. gpt-6.1-sol is about 5x cheaper
    # for 4 index points less (model-selection.md) and produced turns in sessions #48-#50; Sonnet is the
    # Claude fallback. Opus stays only where its edge is claimed (policymaker, evaluator).
    orchestrator: &planning
      - {provider: codex, model: gpt-6.1-sol}
      - {provider: claude, model: claude-sonnet-5-5}
    researcher: *planning
    # Iteration 0005 (sessions #104, #106): codex benchmark sessions hit the engine's 800k unique-input budget
    # after 26-28 turns (cache_read share 5%; role_runtime.unique_input counts codex input minus cache reads),
    # status partial, output unmerged. Claude counts cache reads as free, so a growing history costs far less
    # of the budget. Benchmark work goes Claude-first until measured otherwise; review stays on codex (other family).
    benchmark: *implementation
    policymaker: &measured
      - {provider: claude, model: claude-opus-5-5}
      - {provider: codex, model: gpt-6.1-sol}
    evaluator: *measured
    # Luna dropped from the first slot: audit #43 spent 1.17M luna input with 0 turns and crashed.
    audit:
      - {provider: codex, model: gpt-6.1-sol}
      - {provider: claude, model: claude-sonnet-5-5}
    # Luna is a first-pass filter, not a sole reviewer (model-selection.md). Review starts on another
    # family than the Claude-first implementation and evaluator routes.
    evaluator-verifier: &review
      - {provider: codex, model: gpt-6.1-sol}
      - {provider: claude, model: claude-sonnet-5-5}
      - {provider: copilot, model: gpt-5.6-luna}
    review: *review
    reviewer: *review
policymaker_session:                 # model id (not an alias); bounded by engine.yml policymaker_session_ceilings
  model: claude-opus-5-5
  effort: high
  max_turns: 60                  # every turn resends the prompt; a Policymaker needing more than 60 is investigating too broadly
  timeout_minutes: 90
models:                          # label `model:<alias>` on a task -> model id; `default` when there is no label
  default: claude-sonnet-5-5
  opus: claude-opus-5-5
efforts: [low, medium, high]
ceilings:                        # a task's limits never exceed these; the engine enforces time and turns hard
  job_minutes: 240               # outer cap; starting ordinary role profiles use at most 120 minutes
  iteration_minutes: null
  max_turns: 150
policymaker_triggers:                 # the Policymaker runs after an iteration closes when one fires; it never blocks an iteration.
                                 # A new audit report always calls it. null: off
  every_iterations: 1            # shaper: null needs the Policymaker's orders every iteration (docs/perpetua/engine.md); 5 failed iteration 0007 (issue 100)
  no_progress: 3                 # each time this many more iterations in a row went without an improving change
context:                         # what each model request carries of the session history; bounded by engine.yml context_ceilings
  history_bytes: 40000           # about 10k tokens; every turn is a stateless call resending this (owner note 2026-10-24)
  recent_turns: 5                # these turns in full, older ones as tool/path/status only
limits:                      # kernel hard caps: fix_rounds, successor_generations, merge_conflict_retries 5; backoff 6 steps of 72 h
  fix_rounds: 2              # correction rounds after a failed verification or check
  successor_generations: 3
  merge_conflict_retries: 3
  backoff_hours: [1, 5, 24]  # waits after a rate limit without a reset time
cadence:                     # only stricter than the owner's in engine.yml has an effect
  min_interval_minutes: null
  daily_iterations: null
policymaker_only_roles: [evaluator, audit]   # tasks of these roles come only from the Policymaker's orders
audit_exports_window: 3      # the audit receives the streams of this many iterations before the current one
stream_retention_iterations: null   # keep raw session streams for this many iterations (null: GitHub's 90 days)
startup_token_warning: 100000    # initial documents of any model session; diagnostics never block execution

- Input budget: a session stops `partial/input_budget` at 800k unique input (`role_runtime.py`). Codex counts

- In 0005 and 0006 every order was started twice (issues 109/111 and 110/112: same id, pass 1), so the work is paid for twice; see `.session/history/records/0006.json`.
